Black Designers Dominated NYFW — Behold Every Moment
These are the Black-owned brands that should be on your radar.
Courtesy of Brand
By
Greg Emmanuel
·
Updated February 17, 2022
Getting your
Trinity Audio
player ready…
In the words of Issa Rae, we’re always rooting for everybody Black – including all of the Black designers that showcased at New York Fashion Week 2022. As we reach the end of the official week organized by the CFDA and IMG, we’ve curated a central list of every Black designer that was on the calendar, along with their latest collections.
This February, most designers debuted their Fall/Winter 2022 collections, however some designers did opt to showcase Spring collections. And while traditionally designers host individual fashion shows,
Black in Fashion Council
arranged a showroom for attendees to see several Black designers in one location, with the
IN THE BLK collective organizing a showcase that spotlighted three Black luxury designers on the runway
.
While we missed a couple of our favorite Black designers that didn’t show this season, like
Theophilio
and
Pyer Moss
, we enjoyed seeing the Black designers that returned and new talent that made their NYFW debut.
Discover all of the Black designers that showcased at NYFW ahead.
01
No Sesso
No Sesso
, the genderless, LA-based brand founded by Pia Davis, presented its FW22 collection, “The Girls With Dolphin Earrings”, a collection designed by Davis and Autumn Randolph.
Courtesy of Brand
02
Advisry
Advisry, founded by Keith Herron, debuted its FW22 collection “Sometimes Dancing” – a display of finding Black joy in the midst of chaos and trauma.
Courtesy of Brand
03
Telfar
Telfar
, the unisex brand founded by Telfar Clemens, presented its latest collection, which included new big silhouettes, new bag colors, and new ready-to-wear.
Courtesy of Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images
04
Eugene Taylor
Eugene Taylor
, a unisex brand founded by Letesha Renee, showed its Diana Ross tribute collection at the Black in Fashion Council showroom.
Courtesy of Brand
05
Victor Glemaud
Victor Glemaud
, founded by Victor Glemaud, prseneted his FW22 collection, which was inspired by
Black Girl
, a film directed by Ousmane Sembene.
Courtesy of Brand
06
Who Decides War
Who Decides War
, founded by Ev Bravado and Téla D’Amore, presented its FW22 collection, which consisted of reimagined classics, the brand’s signature distressed details, suiting, and more.
Courtesy of Brand
07
Megan Renee
Megan Renee
, founded by Megan Renee, was one of the new brands that joined the Black in Fashion Council showroom this season. The brand showed its “Higher Ground” collection.
Courtesy of Brand
08
LaQuan Smith
LaQuan Smith
, founded by LaQuan Smith, presented his very sexy FW22 collection.
Courtesy of Fernanda Calfat/Getty Images
09
ASHYA
ASHYA
, founded by Ashley Cimone and Moya Annece, presented its “Heritage Collection” at the Black in Fashion Council Showroom.
Courtesy of Brand
10
House of Aama
House of Aama, founded by Akua Shabaka and Rebecca Henry, presented its FW22 collection, “Bloodroot: Into the Archives, at the IN THE BLK showcase.
Courtesy of JP Yim/Getty Images
11
Nalebe
Nalebe
, founded by Amina Means, presented its FW22 footwear collection, “Stories Through Seasons”.
Courtesy of Brand
12
Lavie By CK
Lavie By CK
, founded by Claude Kameni, presented its latest, colorful collection at the Black in Fashion Council showroom.
Courtesy of Brand
13
Dour Doux
Dur Doux
, founded by Najla and Cynthia Burt, presented its colorful FW22 collection, “Le Nouvelle Mosaique”, which included a selection of menswear, at the brand’s runway show and at the Black in Fashion Council showroom.
Courtesy of Brand
14
CISE
CISE
, founded by Blake Van Putten, returned to the Black in Fashion Council showroom to present new bag silhouettes and new apparel.
Courtesy of Brand
15
KHIRY
KHIRY
, founded by Jameel Mohammed, presented its new collection of fine jewelry, alongside innovative runway looks at the IN THE BLK showcase.
Courtesy of JP Yim/Getty Images
16
Sergio Hudson
Sergio Hudson
, founded by Sergio Hudson, presented its colorful SS22 collection, which was inspired by ’90s TV icons – specifically Cher from the movie
Clueless
, Whitley Gilbert from ’90s sitcom
A Different World
and Lisa Turtle from
Saved by the Bell
.
Courtesy of Brand
17
Tia Adeola
Tia Adeola
, founded by Tia Adeola, presented her latest collection, infused with potent messages, at the Prince George Ballroom.
Courtesy of Brand
18
Third Crown
Third Crown
, founded by Kristin and Kofi Essel, presented its “Edelsteen” collection at the IN THE BLK showcase.
Courtesy of JP Yim/Getty Images
